steps.description: This is a pure machine learning / mathematical inquiry into "solution space rigidity" using small feedforward networks as probes. The plan is to design a numerical experiment: (1) Define a set of analytical constraints (e.g., interpolation conditions on a function space); (2) Vary the number of constraints w; (3) For each w, perform a grid search over hidden layer width N_c to find the minimum width achieving zero violation (max abs error ≤ 1e-3) on held-out constraint points; (4) Record training/validation errors and N_c(w) trend. If N_c remains small and bounded as w increases, the solution space is rigid; if no finite N_c achieves zero violation, it is "fat". Execute with reproducible small networks (e.g., 1–2 hidden layers, activation functions like tanh or ReLU), ensuring all outputs are finite numbers. Use symbolic regression or direct DFT-style scanning methodology to systematically explore capacity vs. constraint count.
